- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — dampen forecast slope downward for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is trending up, model may overestimate continuation — cap forecast growth at 2–3% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive, model often misreads momentum — delay forecast reversal until sentiment stabilizes (wait 2–3 days).
- Model tends to overestimate short-term volatility in high-sentiment periods — smooth 30d forecast by reducing standard deviation by 15–20% if sentiment > 0.2.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 5+ days, model may be overconfident — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- Sentiment decay (e.g., -0.3 to -0.1) often precedes price correction — model should anticipate mean reversion and reduce forecast by 3–7% if sentiment is trending down.
